The Hotel

An 18-room heritage house in the medieval city of Bhaktapur, built around courtyards, Newari craft, and the five elements.

Bhaktapur is called the Museum of Life, and The Nanee is built in its image. Preserved brick lanes, carved windows, and temple squares sit in quiet harmony with a hotel shaped by the same hands and materials: brick, wood, brass, and terracotta, gathered around open courtyards, two minutes on foot from Durbar Square.

    Gastronomy

    Dining at The Nanee follows the rhythm of the seasons and the farms around Bhaktapur. Each morning the kitchen writes the day around what the market brings in. When the season turns, the menu turns with it, so switch the season in the hero and watch today change.

    Today at the Bistro

    “We cook the way this city has always cooked: over fire, by hand, and for the people at the table. Nothing here travels far, and nothing is in a hurry.” · The Kitchen at The Nanee

    Gatherings

    One long table,
    the whole courtyard

    The Community Feast is how Bhaktapur celebrates: food cooked together in the garden, then eaten together at one long table. Weddings, birthdays, reunions, and evenings that simply deserve marking. Bring your people, and the house does the rest, from the first bara off the chulha to stories after dark in Baakha Kuthu, the storytelling room.

    Journal · Notes from the house

    A house built on five elements, stories told by word of mouth, and a stove that still burns.

    Earth, water, fire, air, and space shape every room. In Baakha Kuthu, artisans and storytellers pass on the city's history the Shruti Parampara way. And at the Bara Shop, Newari food is still flipped by hand over the chulha. Come and hear it all in person.

    Letters from the courtyard

    Seasonal menus, storytelling evenings, and first word of feast dates, sent a few times a year and never more.
